What follows Japan’s yen interventions?

Japan bought yen in four episodes in 2022–24. In each one the currency strengthened by the first New York noon quote after the final operation. The April 2024 gain almost disappeared a month later. The July gain grew.

From April 1991 through September 2026, Japan’s Ministry of Finance recorded 364 yen–dollar operation dates. Grouping nearby actions produces 71 episodes. Three comparable periods without intervention were available for 51 of them.

Two 2024 pathsResults by directionMethod and sourcesAll episode dates

Two purchases, two paths

The Ministry bought ¥9.7885 trillion across 29 April and 1 May. Twenty sessions after the first post-operation quote, the yen had retained only 0.27 log percentage points of its 2.47-point initial gain. In July, a smaller ¥5.5348 trillion purchase was followed by a 9.18-point gain over the longer window. Lower yen per dollar means a stronger yen.

What survives comparison with other periods?

For 2022–24, the median first-quote appreciation was 1.86 log %. It exceeded the average change in the three matched periods by a median 1.33 log percentage points. The early sales give a different comparison. Across 51 episodes, the median first move was 0.56 log % in the intended direction. Among the 33 episodes with matches, the median observed move was +0.20 and the median excess was −0.09 log percentage points.

How to read the comparison

Does the yen keep moving in the direction of an official purchase or sale after the initial market response? Compare the first available exchange rate after each episode with later quotes and with periods that began under similar market conditions.

  1. Cluster the transactions. Combine successive yen–dollar operations in the same direction when no more than five New York FX observation sessions separate them. Keep the Japanese Ministry of Finance’s original unit of ¥100 million in the downloadable data. The yen amounts on this page sum the published daily figures. The amount comparison excludes 25 other-currency records. All Ministry operations can trigger an exclusion.
  2. Align the two clocks. The Ministry gives Japanese operation dates. The Federal Reserve’s H.10 series gives New York noon buying rates in yen per US dollar. The baseline is the last observed noon strictly before the first operation date. The first endpoint is the first observed noon strictly after the last operation date. Count another five and twenty observed FX sessions from that endpoint. All changes start from the original baseline. The window includes other news during the episode. Intraday intervention prices are unavailable.
  3. Orient the sign. Calculate 100 times the natural log of the endpoint divided by the baseline. Reverse the sign for purchases of yen. Positive values therefore mean the currency moved in the announced direction. Drop a horizon from the summary whenever another Ministry action took place after the final operation and on or before that horizon’s noon quote date. The ledger retains excluded observations for inspection.
  4. Find comparable windows. Use the same number of FX sessions over the episode. Candidate baselines fall within 731 calendar days of the actual baseline and must have the same Bank of Japan framework at the start of the lookback, baseline, first endpoint and last follow-up. Exclude every candidate with a Ministry intervention from 20 sessions before its baseline through its final follow-up. Compare prior 20-session FX change, daily FX volatility and the US two-year Treasury yield change in basis points. For yields use the latest available observation on or before each endpoint, up to five calendar days old.
  5. Pick three controls. Scale each difference by its standard deviation across eligible windows for that episode. Drop candidates beyond 1.5 standard deviations on any feature. In order of smallest Euclidean distance, select three whose observation spans, including the lookback, do not overlap each other. Controls can be reused across episodes. Excess is the observed signed change less the mean signed change in that episode’s three controls. If three suitable periods cannot be found, only the observed move enters the summary.

The policy-framework screen allows comparison within the same broad Japanese monetary arrangements. It does not control for contemporaneous US or Japanese announcements, volatility after intervention, changing policy settings within a framework, or the authorities’ private reasons for acting. Small cohorts, control reuse and repeated actions limit inference. A move in the intended direction cannot establish that intervention caused it.

Official sources include the Ministry of Finance intervention releases · Historical operations CSV · Federal Reserve H.10 yen per dollar · Federal Reserve H.15 two-year Treasury yield · Bank of Japan framework chronology · QQE, yield-curve control and the March 2024 transition.
